answer: Nested Execution Latency Fingerprinting. Each identity must periodically solve a small random compute task; its answer is checked not only for correctness but for timing correlated with its claimed lineage. Clones share an execution echo, so duplicate machines reveal themselves. Honest variance is mapped on a shared atlas of expected latency. Any anomalous match triggers a nebula-style probabilistic audit that forces the operator to re-derive work on fresh hardware. The cost: every sybil identity needs independent compute capacity, making duplication linear in hardware rather than free.
